data.title: Cyclophosphamide injection
data.summary: V Immunosuppressants · Nitrogen mustard alkylating agent (prodrug)
data.body:
_Injectables · V Immunosuppressants_

**Class:** Nitrogen mustard alkylating agent (prodrug)

## Mechanism of action
- Activated in the liver (CYP2B6, 2C19) to phosphoramide mustard, which cross-links DNA strands (guanine N7) → cell death; cell-cycle non-specific
- Strongly suppresses B cells (antibody production) and T cells
- By-product acrolein causes bladder toxicity

## Pharmacokinetics
- Oral and IV; metabolites excreted in urine — reduce dose in renal failure

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Pemphigus: DCP pulse (dexamethasone–cyclophosphamide; third line in the Derma Desk ladder); also refractory pemphigoid and mucous membrane pemphigoid (ocular)
- Systemic vasculitis (granulomatosis with polyangiitis, polyarteritis nodosa), lupus nephritis, dermatomyositis with lung disease, systemic sclerosis lung
- Lymphoma/mycosis fungoides (oncology), pyoderma gangrenosum (refractory)

## Dose & formulations
- DCP: 500 mg IV on day 1 of each monthly dexamethasone pulse, plus 50 mg orally daily between pulses
- Vasculitis/lupus (IV pulse): 500–1000 mg/m² (or 15 mg/kg) monthly
- Oral: 1–2 mg/kg/day
- Give in the morning with plenty of fluid (2–3 L/day), frequent voiding; mesna with high IV doses

## Adverse effects
- Bone marrow suppression (nadir 8–14 days)
- Haemorrhagic cystitis (acrolein) and bladder cancer (long-term, cumulative) — prevent with hydration and mesna
- Infertility: premature ovarian failure, azoospermia (consider sperm/oocyte preservation)
- Nausea, vomiting, alopecia (anagen effluvium), nail and skin hyperpigmentation
- Infections (including PJP — consider co-trimoxazole prophylaxis), secondary malignancy (leukaemia, lymphoma, skin cancer)
- SIADH, pulmonary fibrosis, cardiotoxicity (high doses)

## Contraindications
- Pregnancy and breastfeeding; active serious infection; bone marrow failure
- Urinary outflow obstruction

## Drug interactions
- Allopurinol: increases marrow toxicity
- Enzyme inducers (phenobarbital, rifampicin) increase toxic metabolites
- Succinylcholine: prolonged apnoea (cyclophosphamide inhibits pseudocholinesterase)

## Monitoring
- CBC weekly to 2-weekly during therapy; urine for blood monthly and then for life (bladder cancer risk)
- Renal function, LFT; pregnancy test; fertility counselling

## Pregnancy & lactation
Contraindicated (old FDA category D) — teratogenic. Effective contraception during and for some months after treatment.

## Viva points
- Prodrug activated in the liver; acrolein → haemorrhagic cystitis; mesna is the antidote for the bladder
- Lifelong urine checks for bladder cancer
- DCP regimen for pemphigus (Pasricha)
- Fertility counselling before starting

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.19 (Cytotoxic agents); Khopkar (Non-steroidal immunosuppressive drugs; DCP pulse). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
